questions.question: Where should shipping papers for hazardous materials be placed?

options.text: At the bottom of the stack.

questions.explanation: Drivers must be able to find hazardous materials papers quickly. These papers must be on top of all other shipping papers.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials, which of these should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Do not use hooks or sharp tools when loading hazardous materials. These tools can damage containers.

questions.question: What does Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table show?
questions.explanation: Column 2 lists the official shipping names and descriptions of hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which agency does a background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts the background check for hazardous materials endorsements.

questions.question: What must you know to choose the right placards?

options.text: The hazard class of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard class of the materials.
questions.explanation: You must know the hazard class, the amount being shipped, and the total weight of all hazardous materials to pick the right placards.

questions.question: How should you load hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Always load hazardous materials away from heat. Heat makes many materials more dangerous.

questions.question: What material should a floor liner be made of when transporting Division 1.1 materials?
questions.explanation: The floor liner must be made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: What must emergency response information include?
questions.explanation: Emergency response information must describe the fire and explosion risks of the hazardous materials.

questions.question: How must placards be positioned?

options.text: Any way, as long as they are visible.
So words and numbers read from left to right.
Within three inches of other markings.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words and numbers read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards must be positioned so words and numbers can be read from left to right. They must be at least three inches away from other markings.

questions.question: When can an improperly placarded vehicle be moved?

options.text: To make room for other vehicles.
If it will travel less than 10 miles.

questions.explanation: A vehicle must have proper placards before it can be driven. An improperly placarded vehicle can only be moved if necessary to protect people or property in an emergency.

questions.question: When transporting radioactive materials, what is important to know?

options.text: Radiation passes through to other packages.
The packages should be carried in the cab.
The packages should be loaded on their side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads around radioactive packages and passes through to nearby packages. Because of this, there are limits on how many radioactive packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: When must a driver take the HazMat knowledge test?
questions.explanation: You must pass the HazMat knowledge test in English and pass a federal background check before you renew your CDL each time.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: How much packaging is needed for the shipment.
Where items can be placed on the trailer.
How to load and unload the material.

questions.explanation: There are nine hazard classes. Each class shows the specific dangers of that material.

questions.question: What does Column 2 of the Hazardous Materials Table show?
questions.explanation: Column 2 lists the correct shipping names and descriptions of hazardous materials.

questions.question: How many identical placards must be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on all four sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: Who must identify the hazard class of materials being shipped?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for identifying the product number, shipping name, hazard class, packing group, and correct packaging, labels, marking, and placards.

questions.question: To choose the right placard for hazardous materials, you must know:

options.text: The hazard classes of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: The hazard classes of the materials.
questions.explanation: Placards are placed on vehicles to show the hazard classes of the materials being carried.

questions.question: If a package is too small for a HazMat label, how should it be labeled?
questions.explanation: If a hazardous materials package is too small for a label, the label can be attached to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: What must you keep in your vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: When transporting chlorine in cargo tanks, you must keep an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in your vehicle.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations are meant to protect:
questions.explanation: Transporting hazardous materials is risky. The regulations protect you, people around you, and the environment.

questions.question: When accepting a package of hazardous materials, a driver should check that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on the packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the shipping papers to the markings and labels on the packages when carrying hazardous materials.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT considered a hazardous material?
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are products that pose risks to health, safety, and property. These include explosives, flammable gases, poisonous gases, and hazardous solids. Rocks are not hazardous materials.

questions.question: How do other drivers know when hazardous materials are being transported?

options.text: By placards posted on the truck.
By flashing lights on the truck.
By the driver waving an arm out the window.

questions.correctAnswerText: By placards posted on the truck.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped placards are placed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials to alert other drivers.

questions.question: If a hazardous materials package is too small for its label, how should it be labeled?

options.text: Tie it with other items and place a paper label on the outside of the bundle.
Attach the label to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
Mark the item with a large orange dot.
Place the item in a box that displays a warning label.

questions.correctAnswerText: Attach the label to a tag that is securely attached to the package.
questions.explanation: If the label will not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: How many placards must be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: At least four identical placards must be displayed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials. Place them on the front, back, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: A driver should ensure that:

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.
The shipping paper is not in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare shipping papers to package markings and labels. Make sure the basic description on the shipping paper matches the markings and labels.

questions.question: What sign might indicate a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
The cargo is picked up from a supermarket.
The cargo is packaged in cardboard boxes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cargo is stored in cylinder tanks.
questions.explanation: Cylinders and drums are often used to hold hazardous materials. Take proper precautions when transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: If a substance is being transported in a reportable quantity, what letters will appear on the shipping paper and package?
questions.explanation: When transporting a substance in reportable quantity, the shipper must display the letters "RQ" on the shipping paper and package.

questions.question: Some areas have restrictions on transporting explosives or hazardous waste. What should you do about these restrictions?

options.text: Usually they are not a concern.
Research them before planning your route.
They only apply if transporting more than 1,000 pounds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Research them before planning your route.
questions.explanation: Before transporting hazardous materials, research any restrictions that apply to the routes you plan to take.

questions.question: If you need to transfer Class 3 flammable liquids to another tank, when should this be done?

options.text: On the roadway as long as no other people are nearby.
Not on a public road, unless it is an emergency.
Secretly so people do not know about the transfer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not on a public road, unless it is an emergency.
questions.explanation: Do not transfer flammable liquids from one vehicle to another on a public road unless there is an emergency. Always warn others about the hazards.
